rounds.q: What year did Yellowstone become the world's first national park?
rounds.why: President Ulysses S. Grant signed the law that created it on March 1 of that year.
rounds.src: National Park Service, Birth of a National Park (Yellowstone, 1872)
rounds.fun: The world's first national park turned up in 1872, signed in on March 1!

rounds.q: How many national parks does the US have?
rounds.why: California has the most with 9, and Alaska is right behind with 8.
rounds.src: National Park Service, National Park System unit list (updated Oct 2026)
rounds.fun: 64 parks to visit, and California and Alaska hold 17 of them between the two.

rounds.q: What % of Americans age 6 and up did an outdoor activity in 2025?
rounds.why: That adds up to a record 183.2 million people taking part in outdoor recreation.
rounds.src: Outdoor Industry Association, 2026 Outdoor Participation Trends Report (2025 data)
rounds.fun: 59% of us got outside, a record 183.2 million people. Fresh air for the win!

rounds.q: How many miles long is the Appalachian Trail?
rounds.why: The official 2026 length is 2,197.9 miles, half a mile longer after a reroute in Virginia.
rounds.fun: 2,197.9 miles of trail, and it grew half a mile in 2026. Lace up!

rounds.q: How many million visits did US national park sites get in 2025?
rounds.why: Great Smoky Mountains was the busiest national park, with about 11.5 million visits.
rounds.src: National Park Service, 2025 visitation statistics (323,014,305 recreation visits)
rounds.fun: 323 million visits, and the Great Smoky Mountains welcomed about 11.5 million.
